decisions.statement: The rules are found in the index.
A rule's code is read from the change the check is handed.
No rule's code is read from the working tree while a change is judged.
A rule the tree no longer holds is judged by the body the change answers for.
Every rule a run loads is compiled once and held for the rest of that run.
A rule's code that does not parse refuses the run.
No rule is judged by what a recovering parse made of a body.
A rule whose code the change carries is judged by the body the change carries.
No rule is judged by the body that rule had before the change.
A rule body the change carries is run before anyone has read that body.
A file is parsed the once and handed to every rule left to judge it.
A rule the file's text excuses is left out before the file is parsed.
A file every mark excuses reaches no parse and no rule.
A mark is read off the rule's own code beside the judging.
The rules sit together under one check rather than each rule apart.
A file two rules refuse is refused by each rule apart.
Each reason names the rule that gave the reason.
A check with no rule at all is refused.
A rule that throws is not caught here.
A file whose bytes are not valid UTF-8 refuses the check rather than passing.
A body the change carries reaches a module that change moves at the path it moves to.

definition: the check refusing a source file with a pattern a syntax rule names
